findings.claim: In 2011 Brazilian inspectors found 15 migrant workers in conditions classed as analogous to slavery in São Paulo workshops making Zara garments, and fined Zara Brasil. Its court challenge failed in 2014 and on appeal, and the case closed in November 2017; the facts are now over ten years old.

NGOs alleged in French complaints from 2021 that Inditex and three other groups sold goods made partly with forced Uyghur labour, which Inditex calls unfounded. Prosecutors dropped a 2021 probe for lack of jurisdiction in 2023, and in February 2025 the Paris appeal court upheld a refusal to open a judicial investigation; a new complaint was announced.

In April 2024 Earthsight alleged that Better Cotton-certified cotton from Bahia estates linked to deforestation and land conflicts reached Zara via Asian suppliers. An audit commissioned by Better Cotton found three of the farms in no breach of its standards; the allegation is not an official finding.

Inditex's own figures, reported by Reuters in March 2025, put its 2024 scope 3 emissions at about 13.4 million tonnes CO2e, slightly above the 2018 baseline, against an SBTi-approved target of a 51% cut by 2030. Transport emissions rose 10% in 2024.

In January 2026 Poland's consumer regulator UOKiK charged Zara over suspected greenwashing in its Join Life communications, such as zero-waste and net-zero claims without stated scope. No decision has been issued; fines could reach 10% of turnover per practice if confirmed.

A study commissioned by the Greens/EFA group in the European Parliament (December 2016) estimated that Inditex's structures in the Netherlands, Ireland and Switzerland reduced its tax by at least €585 million over 2011 to 2014. The report says the techniques are legal.

Inditex has had a global framework agreement with the union federation IndustriALL since 2007. The November 2019 renewal set up a global union committee on freedom of association and collective bargaining across its main production clusters.
The Fundación Amancio Ortega reports a completed programme, run from 2015 to 2025, that invested €310 million in 450 cancer diagnosis and radiotherapy machines installed in Spain's public hospitals.

ecology.reason: Fast fashion at global scale. Inditex's own figures put 2024 supply-chain (scope 3) emissions at about 13.4 million tonnes CO2e, no lower than in 2018, against a target of halving them by 2030. Earthsight has linked Zara's cotton to deforestation in Brazil; this is an allegation, and an audit for the certifier found no breach on the farms it checked.

social.reason: Brazilian labour inspectors found workers in conditions analogous to slavery in workshops making Zara clothes in 2011, and courts upheld the sanctions against Zara Brasil, with the case closed in 2017. A French complaint over Uyghur forced labour remains an allegation with no investigation open. Inditex has a global framework agreement with IndustriALL.

legal.reason: Regulatory record at company level: Brazilian fines against Zara Brasil over slave-like labour in its supply chain, upheld in court and closed in 2017. No personal legal record for Amancio Ortega was found.

unresolved.reason: Poland’s consumer regulator charged Zara with suspected greenwashing in January 2026; no decision yet. In France, courts declined jurisdiction over a forced-labour complaint against Inditex, upheld on appeal in 2025, and a new filing was announced. Nothing personal is pending.

proposal.counterweights: The Fundación Amancio Ortega reports €310 million invested in 450 cancer diagnosis and radiotherapy machines for Spain's public hospitals (2015 to 2025). Inditex has held a global framework agreement with the IndustriALL union federation since 2007.
proposal.rationale: Social 2 to 3: the rubric puts forced-labour findings at 3, and a Brazilian court upheld a slave-like labour finding against Zara Brasil; the case is one workshop network and dates from 2011, which may argue for keeping 2. Legal 0 to 1: regulatory fines upheld in court; a reading of the 2017 ruling as a court finding could support 2. Unresolved 0 to 2: UOKiK charges are pending. Ecology stays 3. Tax finding (f6) is a political group's estimate of legal avoidance, so it informs no score.

results.comment: SOMO/Mind the Gap: 15 immigrants in two São Paulo workshops sewing for Zara, classed analogous to slavery (2011), 48 fines; Zara Brasil lost its case and the appeal, case closed November 2017 (TRT-2 ruling of 7 Nov 2017 cited). Agência Brasil (16 Apr 2014) confirms the 2014 court rejection naming Zara Brasil Ltda. Company level correct.

BHRRC/AFP (17 May 2023): complaints by Sherpa and others against Uniqlo France, Inditex, SMCP and Skechers; the 2021 case was dropped in April 2023 for lack of jurisdiction; Inditex called the accusations unfounded. FashionUnited (Feb 2025): Paris appeal court investigating chamber upheld the May 2024 refusal to open a judicial investigation; a new complaint to another judge was announced. Correctly labelled an allegation.

Earthsight summary links SLC and Horita Bahia cotton (Better Cotton label, deforestation, land conflicts) to Zara via Bangladesh-based Jamuna Group; report published 11 April 2024 per contemporaneous coverage. Better Cotton audit summary (23 Apr 2024): Peterson audit found the three farms checked not in breach of Better Cotton or ABR standards; it does not name Zara or Inditex, so names_subject false is correct.

Reuters (Helen Reid, 14 Mar 2025) read via SRN News (Salem Media), a wire copy with full Reuters dateline and credits; a second syndicated copy (WXER) carries identical figures, so the copy is judged faithful. Scope 3 2024 13,427,762 t vs 2018 13,421,935 t, SBTi-approved 51% cut by 2030, transport emissions up 10%, figures from the annual report.

UOKiK press release (21 Jan 2026): charges against Zara over Join Life green claims such as zero net emissions and zero waste without stated scope; charge stage only, fines up to 10% of turnover per practice. pending_case is correct.

Greens/EFA press release (8 Dec 2016): commissioned research estimates Inditex avoided at least €585 million in 2011-2014 via the Netherlands, Ireland and Switzerland; release states the techniques are legal.

IndustriALL (13 Nov 2019): renewal of the GFA dating from 2007 creates a global union committee on freedom of association and collective bargaining with representatives from Inditex’s six main production clusters. Source is a union release, not a company filing; company_disclosure kept as the closest available evidence type.

Foundation page lists the programme under fulfilled projects, 2015-2025, €310 million, 450 machines for cancer diagnosis and radiotherapy through Spain’s public health system. Self-reported by the foundation.
